headline: New York enacts 1st data center moratorium for 50MW+ centers
summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signs moratorium on large data centers
details: New hyperscale data centers can't set up shop in New York for up to a year now that Governor Kathy Hochul has signed the nation's first statewide moratorium. The order blocks new environmental permits for data centers over 50 megawatts.

The moratorium could last up to a year as the Department of Public Service comes up with standards to assess the expected environmental impacts of data center construction and operation. Hochul's office says this will give the state time to come up with regulations needed to protect residents from rising energy prices and environmental impact.

Hochul is also asking the Department of Public Service to consider creating a way for data centers to invest in the state's energy infrastructure. She plans to push the legislature to roll back sales tax exemptions for large data centers in the state when they're back in session next year.
caption:
New York halts large data center construction for 1 year

New hyperscale data centers can't set up shop in New York for up to a year now that Governor Kathy Hochul has signed the nation's first statewide moratorium. The order blocks new environmental permits for data centers over 50 megawatts.

The moratorium could last up to a year as the Department of Public Service comes up with standards to assess the expected environmental impacts of data center construction and operation. Hochul's office says this will give the state time to come up with regulations needed to protect residents from rising energy prices and environmental impact.

Hochul is also asking the Department of Public Service to consider creating a way for data centers to invest in the state's energy infrastructure. She plans to push the legislature to roll back sales tax exemptions for large data centers in the state when they're back in session next year.
